implementation_notes: In Kotlin the table module is the Exposed Table object: an object Orders : Table declares the schema, and the module's operations are extension functions on it - selectAll().where { ... } returns a Query of ResultRow, which is the record set - while batchInsert/update keep the write side set-oriented. Exposed's DSL is stateless per call, so the single instance is an object with no mutable state, and jOOQ's generated table classes play the same role with compile-checked SQL. Keep per-row behaviour out of the row type if you want a table module rather than a domain model.
pitfalls: Exposed DSL calls execute eagerly: a loop that runs selectAll() per row is an N+1 by construction, so build one query and reduce the rows in Kotlin.

Transactions are explicit: without a transaction { } block above the module, each call can land in its own commit, and nesting the block wrongly splits the module's work; also declare decimal/precision once in the Table object instead of re-rounding money in Kotlin.
